# Skill Template Reference Guidelines for creating new skills from reflection learnings. ## When to Create a Skill Create a new skill instead of updating an agent when the learning: | Criteria | Explanation | |----------|-------------| | **Non-obvious debugging** | Solution required significant investigation (>10 min) | | **Misleading error** | Error message pointed to wrong direction | | **Workaround discovery** | Found workaround through experimentation | | **Configuration insight** | Setup differs from documented approach | | **Reusable pattern** | Would help in similar future situations | | **Trial-and-error success** | Multiple approaches tried before solution | ## Quality Gates Before creating a skill, verify ALL gates pass: ### 1. Reusable - [ ] Will help with future tasks (not just this one instance) - [ ] Applies to similar situations across projects - [ ] Not overly specific to one codebase ### 2. Non-trivial - [ ] Requires discovery, not just documentation lookup - [ ] Took meaningful effort to figure out - [ ] Not immediately obvious from error message ### 3. Specific - [ ] Can describe exact trigger conditions - [ ] Clear symptoms to match against - [ ] Defined scope (technology, version, context) ### 4. Verified - [ ] Solution actually worked - [ ] Tested in the current context - [ ] Not theoretical or untested ### 5. No Duplication - [ ] Checked existing skills in `~/.claude/skills/` - [ ] Checked existing skills in `.claude/skills/` - [ ] Not covered by existing documentation ## Skill File Structure Create at `.claude/skills/{skill-name}/SKILL.md`: ```markdown --- name: {kebab-case-name} description: | {CRITICAL: Include exact error messages, symptoms, technologies} Use when: (1) {trigger condition 1}, (2) {trigger condition 2} Solves: {problem summary} author: Claude Code (auto-generated via /reflect) version: 1.0.0 date: {YYYY-MM-DD} source_session: {session_id if available} confidence: {HIGH/MEDIUM} --- # {Skill Name} ## Problem {Clear description of the problem this skill solves} ## Context / Trigger Conditions Use this skill when you encounter: - {Exact error message if applicable} - {Symptom 1} - {Symptom 2} - {Technology/framework involved} ## Solution {Step-by-step solution} 1. {Step 1} 2. {Step 2} 3. {Step 3} ## Verification How to verify the solution worked: - {Verification step 1} - {Verification step 2} ## Example {Concrete example from the session where this was discovered} ## Notes - {Caveats or edge cases} - {When this might NOT apply} - {Related issues} ## References - {Link to relevant documentation if any} - {GitHub issue if applicable} - {Stack Overflow thread if helpful} ``` ## Naming Convention Generate skill names from the problem/solution: ``` {problem-domain}-{specific-issue} ``` ### Examples | Problem | Skill Name | |---------|------------| | Prisma connection pool exhaustion | `prisma-connection-pool-exhaustion` | | Next.js hydration mismatch | `nextjs-hydration-mismatch-fix` | | Docker compose DNS issues | `docker-compose-network-dns-resolution` | | TypeScript circular dependency | `typescript-circular-dependency-workaround` | | React useEffect infinite loop | `react-useeffect-infinite-loop-fix` | | PostgreSQL connection timeout | `postgres-connection-timeout-configuration` | ### Naming Rules 1. Use kebab-case (lowercase with hyphens) 2. Start with technology/framework name 3. End with problem type (fix, workaround, configuration, etc.) 4. Keep under 50 characters 5. Be specific enough to distinguish from similar issues ## Description Requirements The description field is **critical** for semantic matching. Include: ### Required Elements 1. **Exact error messages** (for matching) 2. **Technology and version** (for context) 3. **Symptoms** (what user observes) 4. **Trigger conditions** (when it happens) ### Example Description ```yaml description: | React hydration mismatch error: "Text content does not match server-rendered HTML" Occurs with Next.js 13+ when server and client render different content. Use when: (1) seeing hydration warnings in console, (2) dynamic content differs between server and client, (3) using client-only libraries on server. Solves: Hydration mismatch causing React to re-render entire component tree. ``` ## Content Guidelines ### Problem Section - Describe what goes wrong - Include exact error messages - Explain impact (why it matters) ### Context Section - List all trigger conditions - Include technology versions - Describe environment (local, CI, production) ### Solution Section - Step-by-step instructions - Include actual commands/code - Explain why each step works - Note any prerequisites ### Verification Section - How to confirm the fix worked - What to look for - Expected behavior after fix ### Notes Section - Edge cases where fix doesn't apply - Related issues - Alternative approaches - Known limitations ## Skill Location ### Project-Level (Default) Create in `.claude/skills/{name}/SKILL.md`: - Can be reviewed before committing - Versioned with the project - Can be moved to global if broadly applicable ### Global-Level If the skill applies across projects, move to `~/.claude/skills/{name}/SKILL.md`: - Available in all projects - User-level persistence - Not project-versioned ## Example Complete Skill ```markdown --- name: nextjs-hydration-mismatch-fix description: | React hydration mismatch error: "Text content does not match server-rendered HTML" Occurs with Next.js 13+ App Router when server and client render different content. Use when: (1) hydration warnings in browser console, (2) dynamic content like dates/times differ, (3) browser-only APIs used during SSR. Solves: Hydration mismatch causing full client re-render. author: Claude Code (auto-generated via /reflect) version: 1.0.0 date: 2026-01-18 confidence: HIGH --- # Next.js Hydration Mismatch Fix ## Problem React throws "Text content does not match server-rendered HTML" or similar hydration errors when the server-rendered HTML doesn't match what React expects on the client. This causes React to discard the server HTML and re-render the entire component tree client-side, defeating SSR benefits. ## Context / Trigger Conditions Use this skill when you encounter: - Console warning: "Text content does not match server-rendered HTML" - Console warning: "Hydration failed because the initial UI does not match" - Using `Date.now()`, `Math.random()`, or similar in render - Accessing `window`, `localStorage`, or `navigator` during SSR - Different timezone between server and client ## Solution 1. **Identify dynamic content**: Find code that produces different values on server vs client 2. **Use client-only rendering for dynamic content**: ```tsx 'use client' import { useState, useEffect } from 'react' function DynamicContent() { const [mounted, setMounted] = useState(false) useEffect(() => { setMounted(true) }, []) if (!mounted) return null // or a placeholder return
{new Date().toLocaleString()}
} ``` 3. **Use Next.js dynamic imports with ssr: false**: ```tsx import dynamic from 'next/dynamic' const ClientOnlyComponent = dynamic( () => import('./ClientOnlyComponent'), { ssr: false } ) ``` 4. **Use suppressHydrationWarning for intentional mismatches**: ```tsx {new Date().toISOString()} ``` ## Verification - No hydration warnings in browser console - Page loads without flicker - Server HTML matches client HTML (check source vs DOM) ## Example In the debugging session, the issue was a `` element showing current date which differed between server build time and client render time. Fixed by wrapping in a mounted check to only render the date client-side. ## Notes - `suppressHydrationWarning` only suppresses the warning, doesn't fix the mismatch - Prefer mounted check or dynamic import over suppressing warnings - For timestamps, consider using relative time (e.g., "2 hours ago") calculated client-side - Server components in Next.js 13+ don't have this issue for static content ## References - https://nextjs.org/docs/messages/react-hydration-error - https://react.dev/reference/react-dom/client/hydrateRoot#handling-different-client-and-server-content ``` ## Skill Creation Checklist Before finalizing a skill: - [ ] Name follows kebab-case convention - [ ] Description includes error messages for matching - [ ] All quality gates passed - [ ] Problem clearly described - [ ] Trigger conditions specific - [ ] Solution is step-by-step with code - [ ] Verification steps included - [ ] Notes cover edge cases - [ ] Created in `.claude/skills/` for review

# /reflect - Self-Improvement Reflection

Analyze the current conversation for corrections, success patterns, and learnings. Extract insights and propose targeted updates to agent files.

**Philosophy**: "Correct once, never again."

## Usage

```bash
/reflect                    # Analyze current conversation
/reflect [agent-name]       # Focus on learnings for specific agent
/reflect on                 # Enable auto-reflection at session end
/reflect off                # Disable auto-reflection
/reflect status             # Show toggle state and metrics
/reflect review             # Review pending low-confidence learnings
```

## Modes

### Standard Reflection (default)

Scan entire conversation for:
- **High confidence**: Explicit corrections ("never do X", "always check Y")
- **Medium confidence**: Approved approaches (user confirmed it worked)
- **Low confidence**: Observations (patterns that worked, not explicitly validated)
- **New Skills**: Reusable techniques, workarounds, debugging patterns worth preserving

### Targeted Reflection (`/reflect [agent-name]`)

Focus analysis on learnings relevant to a specific agent:

# /reflect - Self-Improvement Reflection

Analyze the current conversation for corrections, success patterns, and learnings. Extract insights and propose targeted updates to agent files.

**Philosophy**: "Correct once, never again."

## Usage

```bash
/reflect                    # Analyze current conversation
/reflect [agent-name]       # Focus on learnings for specific agent
/reflect on                 # Enable auto-reflection at session end
/reflect off                # Disable auto-reflection
/reflect status             # Show toggle state and metrics
/reflect review             # Review pending low-confidence learnings
```

## Modes

### Standard Reflection (default)

Scan entire conversation for:
- **High confidence**: Explicit corrections ("never do X", "always check Y")
- **Medium confidence**: Approved approaches (user confirmed it worked)
- **Low confidence**: Observations (patterns that worked, not explicitly validated)
- **New Skills**: Reusable techniques, workarounds, debugging patterns worth preserving

### Targeted Reflection (`/reflect [agent-name]`)

Focus analysis on learnings relevant to a specific agent:
```bash
/reflect code-reviewer      # Focus on code review learnings
/reflect backend-developer  # Focus on backend learnings
/reflect CLAUDE.md          # Focus on global preferences
```

### Toggle Auto-Reflection

```bash
/reflect on                 # Auto-reflect at session end
/reflect off                # Manual reflection only
/reflect status             # Check current state
```

## Implementation

When this command is invoked:

### 1. Check for Toggle Commands

```bash
ARG="${1:-}"

case "$ARG" in
  "on")
    # Enable auto-reflection
    echo "Setting auto_reflect: true in ~/.claude/session/reflect-state.yaml"
    echo "Auto-reflection enabled. Will analyze session before handover."
    exit 0
    ;;
  "off")
    # Disable auto-reflection
    echo "Setting auto_reflect: false in ~/.claude/session/reflect-state.yaml"
    echo "Auto-reflection disabled. Use /reflect manually when needed."
    exit 0
    ;;
  "status")
    # Show current state
    cat ~/.claude/session/reflect-state.yaml 2>/dev/null || echo "No state file found"
    cat ~/.claude/session/reflect-metrics.yaml 2>/dev/null || echo "No metrics found"
    exit 0
    ;;
  "review")
    # Review low-confidence learnings
    echo "Reviewing pending low-confidence learnings..."
    # Continue to reflection with filter
    ;;
esac
```

### 2. Scan Conversation for Signals

Look for these patterns in the conversation:

**High Confidence (Explicit Corrections)**:
- "never", "don't", "stop doing", "wrong", "not like that"
- "always", "must", "required", "the rule is"
- Frustration: "I already told you", "again?"

**Medium Confidence (Approved Approaches)**:
- "perfect", "exactly", "that's right", "yes, like that"
- User accepted output without modification
- Positive acknowledgment of technique

**Low Confidence (Observations)**:
- Patterns that seemed to work
- Inferred preferences from context
- Edge cases discovered

### 3. Classify and Match to Agent Files or Create Skills

For each signal detected:

1. **Determine category**: Code Style, Architecture, Process, Domain, Tools, **New Skill**
2. **For agent updates**: Match to `~/.claude/agents/*/` file, identify section, draft addition
3. **For new skills**: Check quality gates, generate skill using template

**Skill-Worthy Signals** (create new skill instead of updating agent):
- Non-obvious debugging (>10 min investigation, not in docs)
- Misleading error (root cause different from error message)
- Workaround discovered through experimentation
- Configuration insight (differs from standard/documented)
- Reusable pattern (would help in similar future situations)

**Skill Quality Gates** (must pass before creating):
- [ ] Reusable: Will help with future tasks
- [ ] Non-trivial: Requires discovery, not just docs lookup
- [ ] Specific: Can describe exact trigger conditions
- [ ] Verified: Solution actually worked
- [ ] No duplication: Doesn't exist already

### 4. Generate Reflection Report

Produce this exact output format:

```markdown
# Reflection Analysis

## Session Context
- **Date**: [timestamp]
- **Messages Analyzed**: [count]
- **Focus**: [all agents OR specific agent name]

## Signals Detected

| # | Signal | Confidence | Source Quote | Category |
|---|--------|------------|--------------|----------|
| 1 | [extracted learning] | HIGH | "[user's exact words]" | Code Style |
| 2 | [extracted learning] | MEDIUM | "[context]" | Architecture |
| 3 | [skill-worthy pattern] | HIGH | "[context]" | New Skill |

## Proposed Agent Updates

### Change 1: Update code-reviewer

**Target**: `~/.claude/agents/engineering/code-reviewer.md`
**Section**: Review Heuristics
**Confidence**: HIGH
**Rationale**: User explicitly stated this rule

```diff
--- a/~/.claude/agents/engineering/code-reviewer.md
+++ b/~/.claude/agents/engineering/code-reviewer.md
@@ -82,6 +82,7 @@
 ## Review Heuristics

 * **Security**: validate inputs, authn/z flows, encryption, CSRF/XSS/SQLi.
+* **Security**: [new rule from learning]
```

## Proposed New Skills

### Skill 1: [skill-name]

**Quality Gate Check**:
- [x] Reusable: [why]
- [x] Non-trivial: [why]
- [x] Specific: [trigger conditions]
- [x] Verified: [how verified]
- [x] No duplication: [checked against]

**Will create**: `.claude/skills/[skill-name]/SKILL.md`

**Preview**:
```yaml
---
name: [skill-name]
description: |
  [Include exact error messages, symptoms for semantic matching]
  Use when: (1) [condition], (2) [condition]
  Solves: [problem]
---
```

## Conflict Check

- [x] No conflicts with existing rules detected
- OR: Warning - potential conflict with existing rule in [file:line]

## Commit Message

```
reflect: add learnings from session [date]

Agent updates:
- [learning 1 summary]

New skills:
- [skill-name]: [brief description]

Extracted: [N] signals ([H] high, [M] medium, [L] low confidence)
```

## Review Prompt

Apply these changes?
- `Y` - Apply all changes and commit
- `N` - Discard all changes
- `modify` - Let me adjust specific changes
- `1,3` - Apply only agent changes 1 and 3
- `s1` - Apply only skill 1
- `all-skills` - Apply all skills, skip agent updates
```

### 5. Handle User Response

**On `Y` (approve)**:
1. Apply each change using Edit tool
2. Run `git add` on modified files
3. Commit with generated message
4. Update `~/.claude/session/learnings.yaml` log
5. Update `~/.claude/session/reflect-metrics.yaml`
6. Report success

**On `N` (reject)**:
1. Discard proposed changes
2. Log rejection for analysis
3. Ask if user wants to modify any signals

**On `modify`**:
1. Present each change individually
2. Allow editing the proposed addition
3. Reconfirm before applying

**On selective (e.g., `1,3`)**:
1. Apply only specified changes
2. Log partial acceptance
3. Commit only applied changes

### 6. Update Metrics

After each reflection, update `~/.claude/session/reflect-metrics.yaml`:

```yaml
last_reflection: [timestamp]
total_sessions_analyzed: [N]
total_signals_detected: [N]
total_changes_proposed: [N]
total_changes_accepted: [N]
acceptance_rate: [%]
most_updated_agents:
  - agent-name: count
confidence_breakdown:
  high: [N]
  medium: [N]
  low: [N]
```

## Example Session

```
User: /reflect

Claude: # Reflection Analysis

## Session Context
- **Date**: 2026-01-18 10:30:00
- **Messages Analyzed**: 47
- **Focus**: All agents

## Signals Detected

| # | Signal | Confidence | Source Quote | Category |
|---|--------|------------|--------------|----------|
| 1 | Never invent button styles | HIGH | "never come up with button styles on your own" | Code Style |
| 2 | Prefer cursor pagination | MEDIUM | User approved cursor-based approach | Architecture |
| 3 | Use snake_case in Python | HIGH | "we use snake_case for all Python" | Code Style |

## Proposed Changes

### Change 1: Update ui-designer

**Target**: `~/.claude/agents/design/ui-designer.md`
**Section**: Heuristics
**Confidence**: HIGH
**Rationale**: Explicit correction from user

[diff...]

### Change 2: Update api-architect

**Target**: `~/.claude/agents/engineering/api-architect.md`
**Section**: Design Patterns
**Confidence**: MEDIUM
**Rationale**: User approved this approach for pagination

[diff...]

### Change 3: Update backend-developer

**Target**: `~/.claude/agents/universal/backend-developer.md`
**Section**: Code Style
**Confidence**: HIGH
**Rationale**: Explicit style rule from user

[diff...]

## Conflict Check
- [x] No conflicts detected

## Commit Message
```
reflect: add style and pagination learnings

- Use design system tokens, never invent styles
- Prefer cursor-based pagination for large datasets
- Use snake_case for Python identifiers

Extracted: 3 signals (2 high, 1 medium confidence)
```

## Review Prompt
Apply these changes? (Y/N/modify/1,2,3)

User: Y

Claude: Applied 3 changes:
- ~/.claude/agents/design/ui-designer.md
- ~/.claude/agents/engineering/api-architect.md
- ~/.claude/agents/universal/backend-developer.md

Committed: abc123f "reflect: add style and pagination learnings"

Metrics updated:
- Total learnings: 35 -> 38
- Acceptance rate: 92%
- Most updated: code-reviewer (12), backend-developer (9)
```

## Background Execution Mode

When triggered by hooks (PreCompact), reflection runs as a background subagent:

1. Spawns via Task tool with `run_in_background: true`
2. Outputs to project `.claude/reflections/YYYY-MM-DD_HH-MM-SS.md`
3. Updates global index at `~/.claude/reflections/index.md`
4. Does NOT block the session
5. Changes are queued for review (not auto-applied)

### Output Locations

**Project-level** (auto-created, versioned with repo):
- `.claude/reflections/YYYY-MM-DD_HH-MM-SS.md` - Full reflection
- `.claude/reflections/index.md` - Project reflection summary
- `.claude/skills/{skill-name}/SKILL.md` - New skills (project-level for review)

**Global** (auto-created):
- `~/.claude/reflections/by-project/{project}/` - Cross-project aggregation
- `~/.claude/reflections/by-agent/{agent}/learnings.md` - Per-agent learnings
- `~/.claude/reflections/index.md` - Global summary

**Note**: Skills are created in PROJECT `.claude/skills/` so you can:
- Review before committing
- Move to global `~/.claude/skills/` if broadly applicable
- Keep project-specific if only relevant to this repo

### Reflection Output File Format

```markdown
# Session Reflection: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM

## Context
- **Project**: [project name]
- **Branch**: [git branch]
- **Messages**: [count]
- **Trigger**: PreCompact / Manual / UserPrompt

## Signals Detected
[table of signals with confidence levels]

## Proposed Changes
[diffs for each proposed change]

## Pending Review
- [ ] Change 1: [description]
- [ ] Change 2: [description]

## Metrics
- Signals: N detected (H high, M medium, L low)
- Auto-triggered: true/false
```

## Integration

### With /handover

If auto-reflection is enabled (`/reflect on`), the PreCompact hook will trigger reflection before handover when context compaction occurs.

### With Session Health

At 🟡 (approaching limit) health status (70%+ context), the UserPromptSubmit hook injects reminders to run `/reflect`.

## File Locations

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `~/.claude/session/reflect-state.yaml` | Toggle state, pending reviews |
| `~/.claude/session/learnings.yaml` | Log of all applied learnings |
| `~/.claude/session/reflect-metrics.yaml` | Aggregate metrics |
| `.claude/reflections/` | Project reflection outputs |
| `.claude/skills/{name}/SKILL.md` | New skills (project-level) |
| `~/.claude/reflections/` | Global reflection index |
| `~/.claude/skills/{name}/SKILL.md` | Global skills (moved manually) |

## Safety Notes

- **Human-in-the-loop**: Never applies changes without explicit approval
- **Git versioned**: All changes committed, easy to rollback
- **Incremental**: Only adds to files, never deletes existing rules
- **Conflict aware**: Warns if new rule might contradict existing

## Troubleshooting

**No signals detected**:
- Session may not have had corrections or explicit feedback
- Try `/reflect review` to check pending low-confidence items

**Conflict warning**:
- Review the existing rule cited

# Reflect - Self-Improvement Agent

## Mission

Analyze conversations to extract learnings, identify corrections and success patterns, and propose updates to agent/skill files for continual self-improvement. Every correction becomes a permanent improvement.

## Core Philosophy

**"Correct once, never again."**

When users correct behavior, those corrections should be encoded into the agent system so the same mistake is never repeated - across all future sessions.

## Signal Detection

### High Confidence Signals (Explicit Corrections)
- Direct negatives: "never", "don't", "stop doing", "wrong"
- Direct positives: "always", "must", "required", "correct way"
- Explicit rules: "the rule is...", "you should know that..."
- Frustration markers: "I already told you", "again?", "not like that"

### Medium Confidence Signals (Approved Approaches)
- Positive feedback on specific approach: "perfect", "exactly", "that's right"
- User accepted a pattern without modification
- Repeated successful interactions using same technique
- "Yes, like that" or "keep doing this"

### Low Confidence Signals (Observations)
- Implicit preferences inferred from context
- Patterns that worked but weren't explicitly validated
- Edge cases discovered during implementation
- Potential improvements without user feedback

## Learning Categories

| Category | Examples | Target Files |
|----------|----------|--------------|
| **Code Style** | Naming conventions, formatting, patterns | `code-reviewer`, `backend-developer`, `frontend-developer` |
| **Architecture** | Design patterns, structure decisions | `solution-architect`, `api-architect`, `architecture-reviewer` |
| **Process** | Workflow preferences, communication style | `CLAUDE.md`, orchestrator agents |
| **Domain** | Business logic, terminology, rules | Domain-specific agents, `CLAUDE.md` |
| **Tools** | Tool usage preferences, CLI patterns | `CLAUDE.md`, relevant specialists |
| **New Skill** | Reusable techniques, workarounds, debugging patterns | `.claude/skills/{name}/SKILL.md` |

## Skill Creation Detection

Beyond updating existing agents, detect when a **NEW SKILL** should be created.

### Skill-Worthy Signals

| Signal | Criteria | Example |
|--------|----------|---------|
| **Non-obvious debugging** | Solution required >10 min investigation, not in docs | "Fixed by setting obscure env var" |
| **Misleading error** | Error message pointed wrong direction, root cause different | "Error said X but problem was Y" |
| **Workaround discovery** | Found workaround through experimentation | "Framework bug, had to patch" |
| **Configuration insight** | Setup differs from standard/documented approach | "Had to configure Z differently for our stack" |
| **Reusable pattern** | Technique would help in future similar situations | "This approach works for all X problems" |
| **Trial-and-error success** | Multiple approaches tried before finding solution | "Tried A, B, C - only D worked" |

### Skill Quality Gates

Before creating a skill, verify:

- [ ] **Reusable**: Will help with future tasks (not just this one instance)
- [ ] **Non-trivial**: Requires discovery, not just documentation lookup
- [ ] **Specific**: Can describe exact trigger conditions and solution
- [ ] **Verified**: Solution actually worked, not theoretical
- [ ] **No duplication**: Doesn't duplicate existing skill or documentation

### Skill Template

Create at `.claude/skills/{skill-name}/SKILL.md`:

```markdown
---
name: {kebab-case-name}
description: |
  {CRITICAL: Include exact error messages, symptoms, technologies for semantic matching}
  Use when: (1) {trigger condition 1}, (2) {trigger condition 2}
  Solves: {problem summary}
author: Claude Code (auto-generated via /reflect)
version: 1.0.0
date: {YYYY-MM-DD}
source_session: {session_id}
confidence: {HIGH/MEDIUM}
---

# {Skill Name}

## Problem

{Clear description of the problem this skill solves}

## Context / Trigger Conditions

Use this skill when you encounter:
- {Exact error message if applicable}
- {Symptom 1}
- {Symptom 2}
- {Technology/framework involved}

## Solution

{Step-by-step solution}

1. {Step 1}
2. {Step 2}
3. {Step 3}

## Verification

How to verify the solution worked:
- {Verification step 1}
- {Verification step 2}

## Example

{Concrete example from the session where this was discovered}

## Notes

- {Caveats or edge cases}
- {When this might NOT apply}

## References

- {Link to relevant documentation if any}
```

### Skill Naming Convention

Generate skill names from the problem/solution:

```
{problem-domain}-{specific-issue}

Examples:
- prisma-connection-pool-exhaustion
- nextjs-hydration-mismatch-fix
- docker-compose-network-dns-resolution
- typescript-circular-dependency-workaround
```

## Workflow

### 1. Signal Detection Scan

```
Scan conversation for:
- Explicit corrections (high confidence)
- Positive feedback on approaches (medium confidence)
- Patterns that worked (low confidence)
- User preferences expressed
```

### 2. Confidence Classification

| Signal Type | Confidence | Criteria |
|-------------|------------|----------|
| Explicit directive | HIGH | User said "never/always do X" |
| Approved approach | MEDIUM | User confirmed approach worked |
| Observation | LOW | Pattern noticed, not validated |

### 3. Agent File Matching

Map each learning to the most relevant agent file:

```
Learning: "Never invent button styles"
  -> Target: ~/.claude/agents/design/ui-designer.md
  -> Section: Heuristics
  -> Addition: "Always use existing design system tokens; never invent styles"

Learning: "Always check for SQL injection"
  -> Target: ~/.claude/agents/engineering/code-reviewer.md
  -> Section: Review Heuristics > Security
  -> Addition: "Verify all DB operations use parameterized queries"
```

### 4. Propose Changes (Diff Format)

Generate precise additions without rewriting entire files:

```diff
--- a/~/.claude/agents/engineering/code-reviewer.md
+++ b/~/.claude/agents/engineering/code-reviewer.md
@@ -82,6 +82,7 @@
 ## Review Heuristics

 * **Security**: validate inputs, authn/z flows, encryption, CSRF/XSS/SQLi.
+* **Security**: Verify all database operations use parameterized queries (never string concatenation).
```

### 5. User Review

Present all proposed changes for approval before applying.

### 6. Apply & Commit

On approval:
1. Apply changes using Edit tool
2. Git commit with descriptive message
3. Log the learning for metrics

### 7. Log Learning

Record in `~/.claude/session/learnings.yaml`:

```yaml
- timestamp: 2026-01-18T10:30:00Z
  signal: "Never invent button styles"
  confidence: high
  source: "explicit_correction"
  target: "~/.claude/agents/design/ui-designer.md"
  status: applied
  session_id: abc123
```

## Output Contract

**Always produce this exact format:**

```markdown
# Reflection Analysis

## Signals Detected

| # | Signal | Confidence | Source Quote | Category |
|---|--------|------------|--------------|----------|
| 1 | [Learning] | HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW | "[exact quote]" | Code Style/Architecture/Process/Domain/Tools/New Skill |

## Proposed Agent Updates

### Change 1: [Target Agent/File]

**Target**: `[file path]`
**Section**: [section name]
**Confidence**: [HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW]
**Rationale**: [why this change]

```diff
[diff showing addition]
```

### Change 2: ...

## Proposed New Skills

### Skill 1: [skill-name]

**Quality Gate Check**:
- [x] Reusable: [why]
- [x] Non-trivial: [why]
- [x] Specific: [trigger conditions]
- [x] Verified: [how verified]
- [x] No duplication: [checked against]

**Will create**: `.claude/skills/[skill-name]/SKILL.md`

**Preview**:
```yaml
---
name: [skill-name]
description: |
  [Semantic-rich description with error messages, symptoms]
  Use when: (1) [condition], (2) [condition]
---
```

**Full content**: [summary of what skill will contain]

### Skill 2: ...

## Conflict Check

- [ ] No conflicts with existing rules
- [ ] OR: Warning - potential conflict with: [existing rule]

## Commit Message

```
reflect: add [brief description]

Agent updates:
- [update 1]
- [update 2]

New skills:
- [skill-name]: [brief description]

Confidence: [overall confidence]
```

## Review Prompt

Apply these changes? (Y/N/modify)
- `Y` - Apply all changes and commit
- `N` - Discard all changes
- `modify` - Let me adjust specific changes
- `1,3` - Apply only agent changes 1 and 3
- `s1,s2` - Apply only skills 1 and 2
- `all-skills` - Apply all skills, skip agent updates
```

## Safety Guardrails

### Human-in-the-Loop
- NEVER apply changes without explicit user approval
- Always show full diff before applying
- Allow selective application of changes

### Git Versioning
- All changes are committed with descriptive messages
- Easy rollback via `git revert`
- Learning history preserved in commit log

### Incremental Updates
- ONLY add to existing sections
- NEVER delete or rewrite existing rules
- Preserve original structure and intent

### Conflict Detection
- Check if proposed rule contradicts existing rule
- Warn user if potential conflict detected
- Suggest resolution strategy

### Decay Mechanism
- Flag LOW confidence learnings for periodic review
- Track if learnings are being useful
- Suggest removal of outdated/unused rules

## File Locations

| Type | Location |
|------|----------|
| Global Agents | `~/.claude/agents/{category}/{name}.md` |
| Project Agents | `.claude/agents/{name}.md` |
| Global Commands | `~/.claude/commands/{name}.md` |
| Global Instructions | `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` |
| Learnings Log | `~/.claude/session/learnings.yaml` |
| Reflection State | `~/.claude/session/reflect-state.yaml` |

## Metrics Tracking

Track in `~/.claude/session/reflect-metrics.yaml`:

```yaml
total_signals_detected: 42
total_changes_proposed: 38
total_changes_accepted: 35
acceptance_rate: 92%
most_updated_agents:
  - code-reviewer: 12
  - backend-developer: 8
  - CLAUDE.md: 6
confidence_distribution:
  high: 15
  medium: 18
  low: 5
estimated_time_saved: "~4 hours (based on prevented re-corrections)"
```

## Example Mappings

| Signal | Confidence | Target | Section | Addition |
|--------|------------|--------|---------|----------|
| "Never come up with button styles on your own" | HIGH | ui-designer | Heuristics | "Use existing design system tokens; never invent styles" |
| "Always check for SQL injections" | HIGH | code-reviewer | Security | "Verify parameterized queries for all DB operations" |
| User approved cursor-based pagination | MEDIUM | api-architect | Patterns | "Prefer cursor-based pagination for large datasets" |
| "We use snake_case for Python" | HIGH | backend-developer | Style | "Use snake_case for Python identifiers" |
| "Tests should be behavioral, not unit" | HIGH | test-writer-fixer | Philosophy | "Favor behavioral/integration tests over unit tests" |

## Integration with Other Agents

- **code-reviewer**: Learns from review feedback to improve checklist
- **test-writer-fixer**: Learns testing preferences and patterns
- **backend-developer/frontend-developer**: Learns style and architecture preferences
- **solution-architect**: Learns architectural decisions and patterns
- **CLAUDE.md**: Learns global preferences that apply everywhere

## Toggle State Management

State stored in `~/.claude/session/reflect-state.yaml`:

```yaml
auto_reflect: false  # or true
last_reflection: 2026-01-18T10:30:00Z
pending_low_confidence:
  - signal: "Might prefer tabs over spaces"
    detected: 2026-01-15T14:00:00Z
    awaiting_validation: true
```

## Output File Generation

When running in background mode (triggered by hooks), generate output files:

### 1. Project Reflection File

Create `.claude/reflections/YYYY-MM-DD_HH-MM-SS.md`:

```bash
# Ensure directory exists

# Generate filename

FILENAME=".claude/reflections/${TIMESTAMP}.md"
```

### 2. Create New Skills (if detected)

For each skill-worthy signal that passes quality gates:

```bash
# Create skill directory
SKILL_NAME="[kebab-case-name]"
mkdir -p .claude/skills/${SKILL_NAME}

# Write SKILL.md using template
cat > .claude/skills/${SKILL_NAME}/SKILL.md << 'EOF'
---

```

**Important**: Skills are created in PROJECT directory `.claude/skills/` so user can:
- Review before committing
- Move to global `~/.claude/skills/` if broadly applicable
- Keep project-specific if only relevant to this repo

### 3. Update Project Index

Create or append to `.claude/reflections/index.md`:

### 5. Update Per-Agent Learnings (for HIGH confidence only)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Signal Detector for Reflect Skill

Detects correction signals and learning opportunities in conversation text.
Classifies signals by confidence level (HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW) and category.

Usage:
    python signal_detector.py --input conversation.txt
    python signal_detector.py --test  # Run self-tests
"""

import re
import sys
from dataclasses import dataclass
from enum import Enum
from typing import Optional


class Confidence(Enum):
    HIGH = "HIGH"
    MEDIUM = "MEDIUM"
    LOW = "LOW"


class Category(Enum):
    CODE_STYLE = "Code Style"
    ARCHITECTURE = "Architecture"
    PROCESS = "Process"
    DOMAIN = "Domain"
    TOOLS = "Tools"
    NEW_SKILL = "New Skill"
    UNKNOWN = "Unknown"


@dataclass
class Signal:
    """A detected signal from conversation."""
    signal: str
    confidence: Confidence
    source_quote: str
    category: Category
    line_number: Optional[int] = None


# High confidence patterns - explicit corrections
HIGH_PATTERNS = [
    # Negative directives
    (r"\b(never|don't|do not|stop doing|wrong|not like that|incorrect)\b", "correction"),
    (r"\b(should not|shouldn't|must not|mustn't)\b", "prohibition"),
    # Positive directives
    (r"\b(always|must|required|the rule is|correct way)\b", "requirement"),
    # Frustration markers
    (r"(I already told you|again\?|not again|how many times)", "frustration"),
    # Explicit rules
    (r"(the rule is|you should know|remember that|don't forget)", "explicit_rule"),
]

# Medium confidence patterns - approved approaches
MEDIUM_PATTERNS = [
    (r"\b(perfect|exactly|that's right|yes, like that|correct)\b", "approval"),
    (r"\b(good|great job|well done|nice|excellent)\b", "positive_feedback"),
    (r"\b(keep doing|continue with|stick with)\b", "continuation"),
]

# Low confidence patterns - observations
LOW_PATTERNS = [
    (r"\b(maybe|perhaps|might want to|consider)\b", "suggestion"),
    (r"\b(seems like|appears to|looks like)\b", "observation"),
    (r"\b(interesting|good idea|could work)\b", "tentative"),
]

# Category detection patterns
CATEGORY_PATTERNS = {
    Category.CODE_STYLE: [
        r"\b(naming|convention|style|format|indent|case|camelCase|snake_case)\b",
        r"\b(variable|function|class|method|parameter)\s+name",
    ],
    Category.ARCHITECTURE: [
        r"\b(pattern|architecture|design|structure|module|component)\b",
        r"\b(separation|coupling|cohesion|dependency|layer)\b",
    ],
    Category.PROCESS: [
        r"\b(workflow|process|step|procedure|protocol)\b",
        r"\b(commit|branch|merge|review|deploy)\b",
    ],
    Category.DOMAIN: [
        r"\b(business|domain|logic|rule|requirement)\b",
        r"\b(customer|user|client|account|order)\b",
    ],
    Category.TOOLS: [
        r"\b(tool|cli|command|terminal|shell|git|npm|docker)\b",
        r"\b(config|setting|environment|variable)\b",
    ],
    Category.NEW_SKILL: [
        r"\b(workaround|trick|hack|solution|fix|debug)\b",
        r"\b(error|bug|issue|problem)\s+(was|is|fixed|solved)\b",
        r"(took|spent)\s+\d+\s*(min|hour|day)",  # Time investment indicates non-trivial
    ],
}


def detect_confidence(text: str) -> tuple[Confidence, str]:
    """Detect confidence level from text patterns."""
    text_lower = text.lower()

    # Check high confidence patterns
    for pattern, pattern_type in HIGH_PATTERNS:
        if re.search(pattern, text_lower, re.IGNORECASE):
            return Confidence.HIGH, pattern_type

    # Check medium confidence patterns
    for pattern, pattern_type in MEDIUM_PATTERNS:
        if re.search(pattern, text_lower, re.IGNORECASE):
            return Confidence.MEDIUM, pattern_type

    # Check low confidence patterns
    for pattern, pattern_type in LOW_PATTERNS:
        if re.search(pattern, text_lower, re.IGNORECASE):
            return Confidence.LOW, pattern_type

    return Confidence.LOW, "observation"


def detect_category(text: str) -> Category:
    """Detect category from text content."""
    text_lower = text.lower()

    for category, patterns in CATEGORY_PATTERNS.items():
        for pattern in patterns:
            if re.search(pattern, text_lower, re.IGNORECASE):
                return category

    return Category.UNKNOWN


def extract_quote(text: str, max_length: int = 100) -> str:
    """Extract a representative quote from the text."""
    # Clean up the text
    text = text.strip()

    # If short enough, return as-is
    if len(text) <= max_length:
        return text

    # Try to find a sentence boundary
    sentences = re.split(r'[.!?]', text)
    if sentences and len(sentences[0]) <= max_length:
        return sentences[0].strip() + "..."

    # Truncate at word boundary
    truncated = text[:max_length].rsplit(' ', 1)[0]
    return truncated + "..."


def extract_learning(text: str) -> str:
    """Extract the core learning from the text."""
    # Remove common prefixes
    prefixes = [
        r"^(you should|always|never|don't|do not|stop|remember to)\s+",
        r"^(the rule is|note that|keep in mind)\s+",
    ]

    result = text.strip()
    for prefix in prefixes:
        result = re.sub(prefix, "", result, flags=re.IGNORECASE)

    # Capitalize first letter
    if result:
        result = result[0].upper() + result[1:]

    return result


def detect_signals(conversation: str) -> list[Signal]:
    """
    Detect all signals in a conversation.

    Args:
        conversation: Full conversation text

    Returns:
        List of detected signals with confidence and category
    """
    signals = []

    # Split into lines for line number tracking
    lines = conversation.split('\n')

    for line_num, line in enumerate(lines, 1):
        # Skip empty lines
        if not line.strip():
            continue

        # Detect confidence
        confidence, pattern_type = detect_confidence(line)

        # Only record if we found a meaningful pattern
        if pattern_type == "observation" and confidence == Confidence.LOW:
            # Skip generic observations
            continue

        # Detect category
        category = detect_category(line)

        # Extract the learning
        learning = extract_learning(line)

        # Extract quote
        quote = extract_quote(line)

        signal = Signal(
            signal=learning,
            confidence=confidence,
            source_quote=quote,
            category=category,
            line_number=line_num
        )

        signals.append(signal)

    # Deduplicate similar signals
    signals = deduplicate_signals(signals)

    return signals


def deduplicate_signals(signals: list[Signal]) -> list[Signal]:
    """Remove duplicate or very similar signals."""
    seen = set()
    unique = []

    for signal in signals:
        # Create a normalized key
        key = signal.signal.lower().strip()
        key = re.sub(r'\s+', ' ', key)

        if key not in seen:
            seen.add(key)
            unique.append(signal)

    return unique


def format_signals_table(signals: list[Signal]) -> str:
    """Format signals as a markdown table."""
    if not signals:
        return "No signals detected."

    lines = [
        "| # | Signal | Confidence | Source Quote | Category |",
        "|---|--------|------------|--------------|----------|",
    ]

    for i, signal in enumerate(signals, 1):
        lines.append(
            f"| {i} | {signal.signal} | {signal.confidence.value} | "
            f"\"{signal.source_quote}\" | {signal.category.value} |"
        )

    return '\n'.join(lines)


def run_tests():
    """Run self-tests to verify pattern matching."""
    test_cases = [
        # High confidence
        ("Never use var in TypeScript", Confidence.HIGH, Category.CODE_STYLE),
        ("You should always validate inputs", Confidence.HIGH, Category.UNKNOWN),
        ("Stop doing that, it's wrong", Confidence.HIGH, Category.UNKNOWN),
        ("I already told you about this", Confidence.HIGH, Category.UNKNOWN),

        # Medium confidence
        ("Perfect, that's exactly what I wanted", Confidence.MEDIUM, Category.UNKNOWN),
        ("Yes, like that is correct", Confidence.MEDIUM, Category.UNKNOWN),
        ("Keep doing it this way", Confidence.MEDIUM, Category.UNKNOWN),

        # Category detection
        ("Use snake_case for Python variables", Confidence.HIGH, Category.CODE_STYLE),
        ("The architecture should use dependency injection", Confidence.HIGH, Category.ARCHITECTURE),
        ("Always run tests before commit", Confidence.HIGH, Category.PROCESS),
        ("This workaround fixed the issue after 2 hours", Confidence.LOW, Category.NEW_SKILL),
    ]

    passed = 0
    failed = 0

    for text, expected_conf, expected_cat in test_cases:
        signals = detect_signals(text)

        if not signals:
            print(f"FAIL: No signal detected for: {text}")
            failed += 1
            continue

        signal = signals[0]

        conf_match = signal.confidence == expected_conf
        cat_match = signal.category == expected_cat or expected_cat == Category.UNKNOWN

        if conf_match and cat_match:
            print(f"PASS: {text}")
            passed += 1
        else:
            print(f"FAIL: {text}")
            print(f"  Expected: {expected_conf.value}, {expected_cat.value}")
            print(f"  Got: {signal.confidence.value}, {signal.category.value}")
            failed += 1

    print(f"\nResults: {passed} passed, {failed} failed")
    return failed == 0


def main():
    """CLI entry point."""
    import argparse
    import json

    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description='Detect signals in conversation')
    parser.add_argument('--input', '-i', help='Input file to analyze')
    parser.add_argument('--test', action='store_true', help='Run self-tests')
    parser.add_argument('--json', action='store_true', help='Output as JSON')

    args = parser.parse_args()

    if args.test:
        success = run_tests()
        sys.exit(0 if success else 1)

    if not args.input:
        # Read from stdin
        text = sys.stdin.read()
    else:
        with open(args.input, 'r') as f:
            text = f.read()

    signals = detect_signals(text)

    if args.json:
        output = [
            {
                'signal': s.signal,
                'confidence': s.confidence.value,
                'source_quote': s.source_quote,
                'category': s.category.value,
                'line_number': s.line_number
            }
            for s in signals
        ]
        print(json.dumps(output, indent=2))
    else:
        print(format_signals_table(signals))


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

            failed += 1
            continue

        signal = signals[0]

        conf_match = signal.confidence == expected_conf
        cat_match = signal.category == expected_cat or expected_cat == Category.UNKNOWN

        if conf_match and cat_match:
            print(f"PASS: {text}")
            passed += 1
        else:
            print(f"FAIL: {text}")
            print(f"  Expected: {expected_conf.value}, {expected_cat.value}")
            print(f"  Got: {signal.confidence.value}, {signal.category.value}")
            failed += 1

    print(f"\nResults: {passed} passed, {failed} failed")
    return failed == 0


def main():
    """CLI entry point."""
    import argparse
    import json

    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description='Detect signals in conversation')
    parser.add_argument('--input', '-i', help='Input file to analyze')
    parser.add_argument('--test', action='store_true', help='Run self-tests')
    parser.add_argument('--json', action='store_true', help='Output as JSON')

    args = parser.parse_args()

    if args.test:
        success = run_tests()
        sys.exit(0 if success else 1)

    if not args.input:
        # Read from stdin
        text = sys.stdin.read()
    else:
        with open(args.input, 'r') as f:
            text = f.read()

    signals = detect_signals(text)

    if args.json:
        output = [
            {
                'signal': s.signal,
                'confidence': s.confidence.value,
                'source_quote': s.source_quote,
                'category': s.category.value,
                'line_number': s.line_number
            }
            for s in signals
        ]
        print(json.dumps(output, indent=2))
    else:
        print(format_signals_table(signals))


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

def get_state_dir() -> Path:

1→---
     2→name: reflect
     3→description: |
     4→  DEPRECATED: Use the portable skill at toolkit/packages/skills/reflect/ instead.
     5→  This agent file is retained for backwards compatibility during transition.

     7→tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Edit, Write, Bash

    10→---
    11→
    12→# Reflect - Self-Improvement Agent
    13→
    14→> **DEPRECATED**: This agent has been consolidated into a portable skill.
    15→> Use the skill at `toolkit/packages/skills/reflect/SKILL.md` instead.
    16→> This file is retained for backwards compatibility during the transition period.
    17→
    18→## Mission
    19→
    20→Analyze conversations to extract learnings, identify corrections and success patterns, and propose updates to agent/skill files for continual self-improvement. Every correction becomes a permanent improvement.
    21→
    22→## Core Philosophy
    23→
    24→**"Correct once, never again."**
    25→
    26→When users correct behavior, those corrections should be encoded into the agent system so the same mistake is never repeated - across all future sessions.
    27→
    28→## Signal Detection
    29→
    30→### High Confidence Signals (Explicit Corrections)
    31→- Direct negatives: "never", "don't", "stop doing", "wrong"
    32→- Direct positives: "always", "must", "required", "correct way"
    33→- Explicit rules: "the rule is...", "you should know that..."
    34→- Frustration markers: "I already told you", "again?", "not like that"
    35→
    36→### Medium Confidence Signals (Approved Approaches)
    37→- Positive feedback on specific approach: "perfect", "exactly", "that's right"
    38→- User accepted a pattern without modification
    39→- Repeated successful interactions using same technique
    40→- "Yes, like that" or "keep doing this"
    41→
    42→### Low Confidence Signals (Observations)
    43→- Implicit preferences inferred from context
    44→- Patterns that worked but weren't explicitly validated
    45→- Edge cases discovered during implementation
    46→- Potential improvements without user feedback
    47→
    48→## Learning Categories
    49→
    50→| Category | Examples | Target Files |
    51→|----------|----------|--------------|
    52→| **Code Style** | Naming conventions, formatting, patterns | `code-reviewer`, `backend-developer`, `frontend-developer` |
    53→| **Architecture** | Design patterns, structure decisions | `solution-architect`, `api-architect`, `architecture-reviewer` |
    54→| **Process** | Workflow preferences, communication style | `CLAUDE.md`, orchestrator agents |
    55→| **Domain** | Business logic, terminology, rules | Domain-specific agents, `CLAUDE.md` |
    56→| **Tools** | Tool usage preferences, CLI patterns | `CLAUDE.md`, relevant specialists |
    57→| **New Skill** | Reusable techniques, workarounds, debugging patterns | `.claude/skills/{name}/SKILL.md` |
    58→
    59→## Skill Creation Detection
    60→
    61→Beyond updating existing agents, detect when a **NEW SKILL** should be created.
    62→
    63→### Skill-Worthy Signals
    64→
    65→| Signal | Criteria | Example |
    66→|--------|----------|---------|
    67→| **Non-obvious debugging** | Solution required >10 min investigation, not in docs | "Fixed by setting obscure env var" |
    68→| **Misleading error** | Error message pointed wrong direction, root cause different | "Error said X but problem was Y" |
    69→| **Workaround discovery** | Found workaround through experimentation | "Framework bug, had to patch" |
    70→| **Configuration insight** | Setup differs from standard/documented approach | "Had to configure Z differently for our stack" |
    71→| **Reusable pattern** | Technique would help in future similar situations | "This approach works for all X problems" |
    72→| **Trial-and-error success** | Multiple approaches tried before finding solution | "Tried A, B, C - only D worked" |
    73→
    74→### Skill Quality Gates
    75→
    76→Before creating a skill, verify:
    77→
    78→- [ ] **Reusable**: Will help with future tasks (not just this one instance)
    79→- [ ] **Non-trivial**: Requires discovery, not just documentation lookup
    80→- [ ] **Specific**: Can describe exact trigger conditions and solution
    81→- [ ] **Verified**: Solution actually worked, not theoretical
    82→- [ ] **No duplication**: Doesn't duplicate existing skill or documentation
    83→
    84→### Skill Template
    85→
    86→Create at `.claude/skills/{skill-name}/SKILL.md`:
    87→
    88→```markdown
    89→---
    90→name: {kebab-case-name}
    91→description: |
    92→  {CRITICAL: Include exact error messages, symptoms, technologies for semantic matching}
    93→  Use when: (1) {trigger condition 1}, (2) {trigger condition 2}
    94→  Solves: {problem summary}
    95→author: Claude Code (auto-generated via /reflect)
    96→version: 1.0.0
    97→date: {YYYY-MM-DD}
    98→source_session: {session_id}
    99→confidence: {HIGH/MEDIUM}
   100→---
   101→
   102→# {Skill Name}
   103→
   104→## Problem
   105→
   106→{Clear description of the problem this skill solves}
   107→
   108→## Context / Trigger Conditions
   109→
   110→Use this skill when you encounter:
   111→- {Exact error message if applicable}
   112→- {Symptom 1}
   113→- {Symptom 2}
   114→- {Technology/framework involved}
   115→
   116→## Solution
   117→
   118→{Step-by-step solution}
   119→
   120→1. {Step 1}
   121→2. {Step 2}
   122→3. {Step 3}
   123→
   124→## Verification
   125→
   126→How to verify the solution worked:
   127→- {Verification step 1}
   128→- {Verification step 2}
   129→
   130→## Example
   131→
   132→{Concrete example from the session where this was discovered}
   133→
   134→## Notes
   135→
   136→- {Caveats or edge cases}
   137→- {When this might NOT apply}
   138→
   139→## References
   140→
   141→- {Link to relevant documentation if any}
   142→```
   143→
   144→### Skill Naming Convention
   145→
   146→Generate skill names from the problem/solution:
   147→
   148→```
   149→{problem-domain}-{specific-issue}
   150→
   151→Examples:
   152→- prisma-connection-pool-exhaustion
   153→- nextjs-hydration-mismatch-fix
   154→- docker-compose-network-dns-resolution
   155→- typescript-circular-dependency-workaround
   156→```
   157→
   158→## Workflow
   159→
   160→### 1. Signal Detection Scan
   161→
   162→```
   163→Scan conversation for:
   164→- Explicit corrections (high confidence)
   165→- Positive feedback on approaches (medium confidence)
   166→- Patterns that worked (low confidence)
   167→- User preferences expressed
   168→```
   169→
   170→### 2. Confidence Classification
   171→
   172→| Signal Type | Confidence | Criteria |
   173→|-------------|------------|----------|
   174→| Explicit directive | HIGH | User said "never/always do X" |
   175→| Approved approach | MEDIUM | User confirmed approach worked |
   176→| Observation | LOW | Pattern noticed, not validated |
   177→
   178→### 3. Agent File Matching
   179→
   180→Map each learning to the most relevant agent file:
   181→
   182→```
   183→Learning: "Never invent button styles"
   184→  -> Target: ~/.claude/agents/design/ui-designer.md
   185→  -> Section: Heuristics
   186→  -> Addition: "Always use existing design system tokens; never invent styles"
   187→
   188→Learning: "Always check for SQL injection"
   189→  -> Target: ~/.claude/agents/engineering/code-reviewer.md
   190→  -> Section: Review Heuristics > Security
   191→  -> Addition: "Verify all DB operations use parameterized queries"
   192→```
   193→
   194→### 4. Propose Changes (Diff Format)
   195→
   196→Generate precise additions without rewriting entire files:
   197→
   198→```diff
   199→--- a/~/.claude/agents/engineering/code-reviewer.md
   200→+++ b/~/.claude/agents/engineering/code-reviewer.md
   201→@@ -82,6 +82,7 @@
   202→ ## Review Heuristics
   203→
   204→ * **Security**: validate inputs, authn/z flows, encryption, CSRF/XSS/SQLi.
   205→+* **Security**: Verify all database operations use parameterized queries (never string concatenation).
   206→```
   207→
   208→### 5. User Review
   209→
   210→Present all proposed changes for approval before applying.
   211→
   212→### 6. Apply & Commit
   213→
   214→On approval:
   215→1. Apply changes using Edit tool
   216→2. Git commit with descriptive message
   217→3. Log the learning for metrics
   218→
   219→### 7. Log Learning
   220→
   221→Record in `~/.claude/session/learnings.yaml`:
   222→
   223→```yaml
   224→- timestamp: 2026-01-18T10:30:00Z
   225→  signal: "Never invent button styles"
   226→  confidence: high
   227→  source: "explicit_correction"
   228→  target: "~/.claude/agents/design/ui-designer.md"
   229→  status: applied
   230→  session_id: abc123
   231→```
   232→
   233→## Output Contract
   234→
   235→**Always produce this exact format:**
   236→
   237→```markdown
   238→# Reflection Analysis
   239→
   240→## Signals Detected
   241→
   242→| # | Signal | Confidence | Source Quote | Category |
   243→|---|--------|------------|--------------|----------|
   244→| 1 | [Learning] | HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW | "[exact quote]" | Code Style/Architecture/Process/Domain/Tools/New Skill |
   245→
   246→## Proposed Agent Updates
   247→
   248→### Change 1: [Target Agent/File]
   249→
   250→**Target**: `[file path]`
   251→**Section**: [section name]
   252→**Confidence**: [HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW]
   253→**Rationale**: [why this change]
   254→
   255→```diff
   256→[diff showing addition]
   257→```
   258→
   259→### Change 2: ...
   260→
   261→## Proposed New Skills
   262→
   263→### Skill 1: [skill-name]
   264→
   265→**Quality Gate Check**:
   266→- [x] Reusable: [why]
   267→- [x] Non-trivial: [why]
   268→- [x] Specific: [trigger conditions]
   269→- [x] Verified: [how verified]
   270→- [x] No duplication: [checked against]
   271→
   272→**Will create**: `.claude/skills/[skill-name]/SKILL.md`
   273→
   274→**Preview**:
   275→```yaml
   276→---
   277→name: [skill-name]
   278→description: |
   279→  [Semantic-rich description with error messages, symptoms]
   280→  Use when: (1) [condition], (2) [condition]
   281→---
   282→```
   283→
   284→**Full content**: [summary of what skill will contain]
   285→
   286→### Skill 2: ...
   287→
   288→## Conflict Check
   289→
   290→- [ ] No conflicts with existing rules
   291→- [ ] OR: Warning - potential conflict with: [existing rule]
   292→
   293→## Commit Message
   294→
   295→```
   296→reflect: add [brief description]
   297→
   298→Agent updates:
   299→- [update 1]
   300→- [update 2]
   301→
   302→New skills:
   303→- [skill-name]: [brief description]
   304→
   305→Confidence: [overall confidence]
   306→```
   307→
   308→## Review Prompt
   309→
   310→Apply these changes? (Y/N/modify)
   311→- `Y` - Apply all changes and commit
   312→- `N` - Discard all changes
   313→- `modify` - Let me adjust specific changes
   314→- `1,3` - Apply only agent changes 1 and 3
   315→- `s1,s2` - Apply only skills 1 and 2
   316→- `all-skills` - Apply all skills, skip agent updates

   318→
   319→## Safety Guardrails
   320→
   321→### Human-in-the-Loop
   322→- NEVER apply changes without explicit user approval
   323→- Always show full diff before applying
   324→- Allow selective application of changes
   325→
   326→### Git Versioning
   327→- All changes are committed with descriptive messages
   328→- Easy rollback via `git revert`
   329→- Learning history preserved in commit log
   330→
   331→### Incremental Updates
   332→- ONLY add to existing sections
   333→- NEVER delete or rewrite existing rules
   334→- Preserve original structure and intent
   335→
   336→### Conflict Detection

   338→- Warn user if potential conflict detected
   339→- Suggest resolution strategy
   340→
   341→### Decay Mechanism
   342→- Flag LOW confidence learnings for periodic review
   343→- Track if learnings are being useful
   344→- Suggest removal of outdated/unused rules
   345→
   346→## File Locations
   347→
   348→| Type | Location |

   376→
   377→## Example Mappings

   387→## Integration with Other Agents

   395→## Toggle State Management

content.content:
1→---
     2→name: reflect
     3→description: |
     4→  Self-improvement through conversation analysis. Extracts learnings from
     5→  corrections and success patterns, proposes updates to agent files or
     6→  creates new skills. Philosophy: "Correct once, never again."
     7→
     8→  Use when: (1) User explicitly corrects behavior ("never do X", "always Y"),
     9→  (2) Session ending or context compaction, (3) User requests /reflect,
    10→  (4) Successful pattern worth preserving.
    11→version: 2.0.0
    12→author: Claude Code Toolkit
    13→allowed-tools:
    14→  - Read
    15→  - Write
    16→  - Edit
    17→  - Grep
    18→  - Glob
    19→  - Bash
    20→---
    21→
    22→# Reflect - Self-Improvement Skill
    23→
    24→## Quick Reference
    25→
    26→| Command | Action |
    27→|---------|--------|
    28→| `/reflect` | Analyze conversation for learnings |
    29→| `/reflect on` | Enable auto-reflection |
    30→| `/reflect off` | Disable auto-reflection |
    31→| `/reflect status` | Show state and metrics |
    32→| `/reflect review` | Review low-confidence learnings |
    33→| `/reflect [agent]` | Focus on specific agent |
    34→
    35→## Core Philosophy
    36→
    37→**"Correct once, never again."**
    38→
    39→When users correct behavior, those corrections become permanent improvements encoded into the agent system - across all future sessions.
    40→
    41→## Workflow
    42→
    43→### Step 1: Initialize State
    44→
    45→Check and initialize state files using the state manager:
    46→
    47→```bash
    48→# Check for existing state
    49→python scripts/state_manager.py init
    50→
    51→# State directory is configurable via REFLECT_STATE_DIR env var
    52→# Default: ~/.reflect/ (portable) or ~/.claude/session/ (Claude Code)
    53→```
    54→
    55→State includes:
    56→- `reflect-state.yaml` - Toggle state, pending reviews
    57→- `reflect-metrics.yaml` - Aggregate metrics
    58→- `learnings.yaml` - Log of all applied learnings
    59→
    60→### Step 2: Scan Conversation for Signals
    61→
    62→Use the signal detector to identify learnings:
    63→
    64→```bash
    65→python scripts/signal_detector.py --input conversation.txt
    66→```
    67→
    68→#### Signal Confidence Levels
    69→
    70→| Confidence | Triggers | Examples |
    71→|------------|----------|----------|
    72→| **HIGH** | Explicit corrections | "never", "always", "wrong", "stop", "the rule is" |
    73→| **MEDIUM** | Approved approaches | "perfect", "exactly", accepted output |
    74→| **LOW** | Observations | Patterns that worked, not validated |
    75→
    76→See [signal_patterns.md](references/signal_patterns.md) for full detection rules.
    77→
    78→### Step 3: Classify & Match to Target Files
    79→
    80→Map each signal to the appropriate target:
    81→
    82→**Learning Categories:**
    83→
    84→| Category | Target Files |
    85→|----------|--------------|
    86→| Code Style | `code-reviewer`, `backend-developer`, `frontend-developer` |
    87→| Architecture | `solution-architect`, `api-architect`, `architecture-reviewer` |
    88→| Process | `CLAUDE.md`, orchestrator agents |
    89→| Domain | Domain-specific agents, `CLAUDE.md` |
    90→| Tools | `CLAUDE.md`, relevant specialists |
    91→| New Skill | `.claude/skills/{name}/SKILL.md` |
    92→
    93→See [agent_mappings.md](references/agent_mappings.md) for mapping rules.
    94→
    95→### Step 4: Check for Skill-Worthy Signals
    96→
    97→Some learnings should become new skills rather than agent updates:
    98→
    99→**Skill-Worthy Criteria:**
   100→- Non-obvious debugging (>10 min investigation)
   101→- Misleading error (root cause different from message)
   102→- Workaround discovered through experimentation
   103→- Configuration insight (differs from documented)
   104→- Reusable pattern (helps in similar situations)
   105→
   106→**Quality Gates (must pass all):**
   107→- [ ] Reusable: Will help with future tasks
   108→- [ ] Non-trivial: Requires discovery, not just docs
   109→- [ ] Specific: Can describe exact trigger conditions
   110→- [ ] Verified: Solution actually worked
   111→- [ ] No duplication: Doesn't exist already
   112→
   113→See [skill_template.md](references/skill_template.md) for skill creation guidelines.
   114→
   115→### Step 5: Generate Proposals
   116→
   117→Produce output in this format:
   118→
   119→```markdown
   120→# Reflection Analysis
   121→
   122→## Session Context
   123→- **Date**: [timestamp]
   124→- **Messages Analyzed**: [count]
   125→- **Focus**: [all agents OR specific agent name]
   126→
   127→## Signals Detected
   128→
   129→| # | Signal | Confidence | Source Quote | Category |
   130→|---|--------|------------|--------------|----------|
   131→| 1 | [learning] | HIGH | "[exact words]" | Code Style |
   132→| 2 | [learning] | MEDIUM | "[context]" | Architecture |
   133→
   134→## Proposed Agent Updates
   135→
   136→### Change 1: Update [agent-name]
   137→
   138→**Target**: `[file path]`
   139→**Section**: [section name]
   140→**Confidence**: [HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW]
   141→**Rationale**: [why this change]
   142→
   143→```diff
   144→--- a/path/to/agent.md
   145→+++ b/path/to/agent.md
   146→@@ -82,6 +82,7 @@
   147→ ## Section
   148→
   149→ * Existing rule
   150→+* New rule from learning
   151→```
   152→
   153→## Proposed New Skills
   154→
   155→### Skill 1: [skill-name]
   156→
   157→**Quality Gate Check**:
   158→- [x] Reusable: [why]
   159→- [x] Non-trivial: [why]
   160→- [x] Specific: [trigger conditions]
   161→- [x] Verified: [how verified]
   162→- [x] No duplication: [checked against]
   163→
   164→**Will create**: `.claude/skills/[skill-name]/SKILL.md`
   165→
   166→## Conflict Check
   167→
   168→- [x] No conflicts with existing rules detected
   169→- OR: Warning - potential conflict with [file:line]
   170→
   171→## Commit Message
   172→
   173→```
   174→reflect: add learnings from session [date]
   175→
   176→Agent updates:
   177→- [learning 1 summary]
   178→
   179→New skills:
   180→- [skill-name]: [brief description]
   181→
   182→Extracted: [N] signals ([H] high, [M] medium, [L] low confidence)
   183→```
   184→
   185→## Review Prompt
   186→
   187→Apply these changes?
   188→- `Y` - Apply all changes and commit
   189→- `N` - Discard all changes
   190→- `modify` - Adjust specific changes
   191→- `1,3` - Apply only changes 1 and 3
   192→- `s1` - Apply only skill 1
   193→- `all-skills` - Apply all skills, skip agent updates
   194→```
   195→
   196→### Step 6: Handle User Response
   197→
   198→**On `Y` (approve):**
   199→1. Apply each change using Edit tool
   200→2. Run `git add` on modified files
   201→3. Commit with generated message
   202→4. Update learnings log
   203→5. Update metrics
   204→
   205→**On `N` (reject):**
   206→1. Discard proposed changes
   207→2. Log rejection for analysis
   208→3. Ask if user wants to modify any signals
   209→
   210→**On `modify`:**
   211→1. Present each change individually
   212→2. Allow editing the proposed addition
   213→3. Reconfirm before applying
   214→
   215→**On selective (e.g., `1,3`):**
   216→1. Apply only specified changes
   217→2. Log partial acceptance
   218→3. Commit only applied changes
   219→
   220→### Step 7: Update Metrics
   221→
   222→```bash
   223→python scripts/metrics_updater.py --accepted 3 --rejected 1 --confidence high:2,medium:1
   224→```
   225→
   226→## Toggle Commands
   227→
   228→### Enable Auto-Reflection
   229→
   230→```bash
   231→/reflect on
   232→# Sets auto_reflect: true in state file
   233→# Will trigger on PreCompact hook
   234→```
   235→
   236→### Disable Auto-Reflection
   237→
   238→```bash
   239→/reflect off
   240→# Sets auto_reflect: false in state file
   241→```
   242→
   243→### Check Status
   244→
   245→```bash
   246→/reflect status
   247→# Shows current state and metrics
   248→```
   249→
   250→### Review Pending
   251→
   252→```bash
   253→/reflect review
   254→# Shows low-confidence learnings awaiting validation
   255→```
   256→
   257→## Output Locations
   258→
   259→**Project-level (versioned with repo):**
   260→- `.claude/reflections/YYYY-MM-DD_HH-MM-SS.md` - Full reflection
   261→- `.claude/reflections/index.md` - Project summary
   262→- `.claude/skills/{name}/SKILL.md` - New skills
   263→
   264→**Global (user-level):**
   265→- `~/.claude/reflections/by-project/{project}/` - Cross-project
   266→- `~/.claude/reflections/by-agent/{agent}/learnings.md` - Per-agent
   267→- `~/.claude/reflections/index.md` - Global summary
   268→
   269→## Safety Guardrails
   270→
   271→### Human-in-the-Loop
   272→- NEVER apply changes without explicit user approval
   273→- Always show full diff before applying
   274→- Allow selective application
   275→
   276→### Git Versioning
   277→- All changes committed with descriptive messages
   278→- Easy rollback via `git revert`
   279→- Learning history preserved
   280→
   281→### Incremental Updates
   282→- ONLY add to existing sections
   283→- NEVER delete or rewrite existing rules
   284→- Preserve original structure
   285→
   286→### Conflict Detection
   287→- Check if proposed rule contradicts existing
   288→- Warn user if conflict detected
   289→- Suggest resolution strategy
   290→
   291→## Integration
   292→
   293→### With /handover
   294→If auto-reflection is enabled, PreCompact hook triggers reflection before handover.
   295→
   296→### With Session Health
   297→At 70%+ context (Yellow status), reminders to run `/reflect` are injected.
   298→
   299→## Portability
   300→
   301→This skill works with any LLM tool that supports:
   302→- File read/write operations
   303→- Text pattern matching
   304→- Git operations (optional, for commits)
   305→
   306→### Configurable State Location
   307→
   308→```bash
   309→# Set custom state directory
   310→export REFLECT_STATE_DIR=/path/to/state
   311→
   312→# Or use default
   313→# ~/.reflect/ (portable default)
   314→# ~/.claude/session/ (Claude Code default)
   315→```
   316→
   317→### No Task Tool Dependency
   318→
   319→Unlike the previous agent-based approach, this skill executes directly without spawning subagents. The LLM reads SKILL.md and follows the workflow.
   320→
   321→### Git Operations Optional
   322→
   323→Commits are wrapped with availability checks - if not in a git repo, changes are still saved but not committed.
   324→
   325→## Troubleshooting
   326→
   327→**No signals detected:**
   328→- Session may not have had corrections
   329→- Try `/reflect review` to check pending items
   330→
   331→**Conflict warning:**
   332→- Review the existing rule cited
   333→- Decide if new rule should override
   334→- Can modify before applying
   335→
   336→**Agent file not found:**
   337→- Check agent name spelling
   338→- Use `/reflect status` to see available targets
   339→- May need to create agent file first
   340→
   341→## File Structure
   342→
   343→```
   344→reflect/
   345→├── SKILL.md                      # This file
   346→├── scripts/
   347→│   ├── state_manager.py          # State file CRUD
   348→│   ├── signal_detector.py        # Pattern matching
   349→│   └── metrics_updater.py        # Metrics aggregation
   350→├── references/
   351→│   ├── signal_patterns.md        # Detection rules
   352→│   ├── agent_mappings.md         # Target mappings
   353→│   └── skill_template.md         # Skill generation
   354→└── assets/
   355→    ├── reflection_template.md    # Output template
   356→    └── learnings_schema.yaml     # Schema definition
   357→```

1→#!/usr/bin/env python3
     2→"""
     3→State Manager for Reflect Skill
     4→
     5→Manages state files for reflection tracking including:
     6→- reflect-state.yaml: Toggle state, pending reviews
     7→- reflect-metrics.yaml: Aggregate metrics
     8→- learnings.yaml: Log of applied learnings
     9→
    10→State directory is configurable via REFLECT_STATE_DIR env var.
    11→Defaults to ~/.reflect/ for portability or ~/.claude/session/ for Claude Code.
    12→"""
    13→
    14→import os
    15→import sys
    16→from datetime import datetime
    17→from pathlib import Path
    18→from typing import Any
    19→
    20→try:
    21→    import yaml
    22→except ImportError:
    23→    print("PyYAML required. Install with: pip install pyyaml")
    24→    sys.exit(1)
    25→
    26→
    27→def get_state_dir() -> Path:
    28→    """Return state directory, configurable via env or default."""
    29→    custom_dir = os.environ.get('REFLECT_STATE_DIR')
    30→    if custom_dir:
    31→        return Path(custom_dir).expanduser()
    32→
    33→    # Check for Claude Code installation
    34→    claude_session = Path.home() / '.claude' / 'session'
    35→    if claude_session.exists():
    36→        return claude_session
    37→
    38→    # Portable default
    39→    return Path.home() / '.reflect'
    40→
    41→
    42→def ensure_state_dir() -> Path:
    43→    """Create state directory if it doesn't exist."""
    44→    state_dir = get_state_dir()
    45→    state_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    46→    return state_dir
    47→
    48→
    49→def get_state_file() -> Path:
    50→    """Return path to reflect-state.yaml."""
    51→    return get_state_dir() / 'reflect-state.yaml'
    52→
    53→
    54→def get_metrics_file() -> Path:
    55→    """Return path to reflect-metrics.yaml."""
    56→    return get_state_dir() / 'reflect-metrics.yaml'
    57→
    58→
    59→def get_learnings_file() -> Path:
    60→    """Return path to learnings.yaml."""
    61→    return get_state_dir() / 'learnings.yaml'
    62→
    63→
    64→def load_yaml(path: Path) -> dict:
    65→    """Load YAML file, return empty dict if not found."""
    66→    if not path.exists():
    67→        return {}
    68→    with open(path, 'r') as f:
    69→        return yaml.safe_load(f) or {}
    70→
    71→
    72→def save_yaml(path: Path, data: dict) -> None:
    73→    """Save data to YAML file."""
    74→    ensure_state_dir()
    75→    with open(path, 'w') as f:
    76→        yaml.dump(data, f, default_flow_style=False, sort_keys=False)
    77→
    78→
    79→def init_state() -> dict:
    80→    """Initialize or load state from state directory."""
    81→    state_file = get_state_file()
    82→
    83→    if state_file.exists():
    84→        state = load_yaml(state_file)
    85→        print(f"Loaded existing state from {state_file}")
    86→        return state
    87→
    88→    # Create default state
    89→    default_state = {
    90→        'auto_reflect': False,
    91→        'last_reflection': None,
    92→        'pending_low_confidence': []
    93→    }
    94→    save_yaml(state_file, default_state)
    95→    print(f"Initialized new state at {state_file}")
    96→    return default_state
    97→
    98→
    99→def get_state() -> dict:
   100→    """Get current state without modifying."""
   101→    return load_yaml(get_state_file())
   102→
   103→
   104→def set_auto_reflect(enabled: bool) -> None:
   105→    """Enable or disable auto-reflection."""
   106→    state = get_state()
   107→    state['auto_reflect'] = enabled
   108→    save_yaml(get_state_file(), state)
   109→    status = "enabled" if enabled else "disabled"
   110→    print(f"Auto-reflection {status}")
   111→
   112→
   113→def update_last_reflection() -> None:
   114→    """Update last_reflection timestamp."""
   115→    state = get_state()
   116→    state['last_reflection'] = datetime.now().isoformat()
   117→    save_yaml(get_state_file(), state)
   118→
   119→
   120→def add_pending_low_confidence(signal: dict) -> None:
   121→    """Add signal to pending review queue."""
   122→    state = get_state()
   123→    pending = state.get('pending_low_confidence', [])
   124→    pending.append({
   125→        'signal': signal.get('signal', ''),
   126→        'detected': datetime.now().isoformat(),
   127→        'awaiting_validation': True,
   128→        'source_quote': signal.get('source_quote', ''),
   129→        'category': signal.get('category', 'Unknown')
   130→    })
   131→    state['pending_low_confidence'] = pending
   132→    save_yaml(get_state_file(), state)
   133→
   134→
   135→def get_pending_reviews() -> list:
   136→    """Get all pending low-confidence learnings."""
   137→    state = get_state()
   138→    return state.get('pending_low_confidence', [])
   139→
   140→
   141→def clear_pending_review(index: int) -> bool:
   142→    """Remove a pending review by index."""
   143→    state = get_state()
   144→    pending = state.get('pending_low_confidence', [])
   145→    if 0 <= index < len(pending):
   146→        pending.pop(index)
   147→        state['pending_low_confidence'] = pending
   148→        save_yaml(get_state_file(), state)
   149→        return True
   150→    return False
   151→
   152→
   153→def add_learning(learning: dict) -> None:
   154→    """Add a learning to the learnings log."""
   155→    learnings_file = get_learnings_file()
   156→    learnings = load_yaml(learnings_file)
   157→
   158→    if 'entries' not in learnings:
   159→        learnings['entries'] = []
   160→
   161→    learnings['entries'].append({
   162→        'timestamp': datetime.now().isoformat(),
   163→        'signal': learning.get('signal', ''),
   164→        'confidence': learning.get('confidence', 'unknown'),
   165→        'source': learning.get('source', ''),
   166→        'target': learning.get('target', ''),
   167→        'status': learning.get('status', 'applied'),
   168→        'session_id': learning.get('session_id', '')
   169→    })
   170→
   171→    save_yaml(learnings_file, learnings)
   172→
   173→
   174→def show_status() -> None:
   175→    """Print current state and metrics."""
   176→    state = get_state()
   177→    metrics = load_yaml(get_metrics_file())
   178→
   179→    print("\n=== Reflect Status ===\n")
   180→    print(f"State Directory: {get_state_dir()}")
   181→    print(f"Auto-Reflect: {'Enabled' if state.get('auto_reflect') else 'Disabled'}")
   182→    print(f"Last Reflection: {state.get('last_reflection', 'Never')}")
   183→
   184→    pending = state.get('pending_low_confidence', [])
   185→    print(f"Pending Reviews: {len(pending)}")
   186→
   187→    if metrics:
   188→        print(f"\n=== Metrics ===\n")
   189→        print(f"Total Sessions: {metrics.get('total_sessions_analyzed', 0)}")
   190→        print(f"Signals Detected: {metrics.get('total_signals_detected', 0)}")
   191→        print(f"Changes Proposed: {metrics.get('total_changes_proposed', 0)}")
   192→        print(f"Changes Accepted: {metrics.get('total_changes_accepted', 0)}")
   193→        print(f"Acceptance Rate: {metrics.get('acceptance_rate', 0)}%")
   194→
   195→
   196→def main():
   197→    """CLI entry point."""
   198→    import argparse
   199→
   200→    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description='Reflect State Manager')
   201→    parser.add_argument('command', choices=['init', 'status', 'on', 'off', 'pending'],
   202→                       help='Command to execute')
   203→
   204→    args = parser.parse_args()
   205→
   206→    if args.command == 'init':
   207→        init_state()
   208→    elif args.command == 'status':
   209→        show_status()
   210→    elif args.command == 'on':
   211→        set_auto_reflect(True)
   212→    elif args.command == 'off':
   213→        set_auto_reflect(False)
   214→    elif args.command == 'pending':
   215→        pending = get_pending_reviews()
   216→        if not pending:
   217→            print("No pending low-confidence learnings.")
   218→        else:
   219→            print(f"\n=== Pending Reviews ({len(pending)}) ===\n")
   220→            for i, item in enumerate(pending):
   221→                print(f"{i+1}. {item.get('signal')}")
   222→                print(f"   Detected: {item.get('detected')}")
   223→                print(f"   Quote: \"{item.get('source_quote', 'N/A')}\"")
   224→                print()
   225→
   226→
   227→if __name__ == '__main__':
   228→    main()
   229→
